title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 268
paragraphs: But whence each of the gods had his birth, or whether they all existed from the beginning, and what forms they have — these things they did not learn until yesterday, so to speak, or the day before. For Hesiod and Homer were, I suppose, four hundred years before my time, and no more; and it is these two who made a theogony for the Hellenes, gave the titles to the gods, assigned them their honours and their arts, and set forth their forms. The poets who are said to have lived before these men were, in my opinion, really after them. Of these things the first are said by the priestesses of Dodona, and the latter — those concerning Hesiod and Homer — by myself.
